answer: An umber walnut grove guards an agent economy with shell-cracking trials: every new identity must crack walnuts one shell at a time, and the trial grows factorially, so the first fake cracks 1 walnut, the second 2, the third 6, the tenth 3,628,800 and the twentieth 2,432,902,008,176,640,000, and twenty fakes together crack 2,561,327,494,111,820,313 walnuts. Bulk farming fails because one zephyr carries a single nutcracker and each shell must crack before the next is handed over, so no walnut can be cracked in parallel or bought; like a squirrel hoarding nuts one by one, never in bulk.
